text.p: Following are highlights of the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Some 200,000 visitors arrived on the Adriatic coast over the weekend.
- Up to 32,000 displaced people whose homes have been rebuilt are to be stripped of their refugee status over the next six months.
- If I become leader of the Croatian Social-Liberal party, the HSLS will not serve as the saviour of minor political parties, says a member of HSLS Drazen Budisa in an interview.
- Wine on tap is one of the suggestions of tourist workers who are trying to combat the dropping sales of wine along the coast during the tourist season.
- Foreign debt rises by $150 million to $4.99 billion in April 1997, compared to the closing figure for 1996.
- The Pope appoints Josip Bozanic the new Zagreb archbishop to replace retired cardinal Franjo Kuharic.

- Croatian women in society feature: Women are a minority regarding high flying positions, but a majority where housework is concerned. They do the house chores by themselves in some 84 percent of Croatian households.
- Croatian Electricity Board vows to pay damages after its workers cut down scores of trees in Podsusedsko Dolje near Zagreb due to the woods blocking the transmission lines' path.
- A 14-year-old boy drowns in Zagreb's lake Jarun as life guards fail to save him in time.
- Bed and breakfast places along the coast that died out completely during the war years may be rejuvenated due to the number of visitors expected this summer.
- The number of requests submitted for the construction of small airports outstrips the actual number of Croatia Airlines aircraft. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
